summary: A stranger can go from Find jobs to a first answer in 12 steps and 7 clicks, with one human wait (approval) whose length nobody measures. The job page is honest about what it does not show and never leaks the site, and the simulation package opens cleanly in USD tools. The biggest gaps: a reply to the introduction email reaches Blueprint instead of the site, the packet gives only the country, the new-job email says nothing about the job and never announces Ready to test, and the package is unusable in MuJoCo or mesh tools. The application, the password sign-up and the second Terms agreement can mostly go, while the one approval stays because the site agreed to share only with approved companies.

findings.title: A reply to the introduction email reaches Blueprint, not the site
findings.today: The introduction row stores the site's email as Reply-To, but every outbox send uses Reply-To hello@tryblueprint.io. A lead who presses Reply writes to Blueprint. A test pins the override, and the introduction test checks only the stored row.
findings.should: Pressing Reply on the introduction email writes to the other side.
findings.proposal: In captureOutbox deliver, for the two introduction kinds, pass entry.replyTo to sendEmail instead of the fixed identity's replyTo; update capture-outbox.test.ts:209 and add a send-time assertion to the introduction test.
findings.user_result: The company reaches the site with one Reply; Blueprint is not a relay.
findings.risk: Replies no longer reach Blueprint, so the owner loses sight of early conversations; outcome questions still record what happened.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine: Blueprint gives each side the other's name and contact details; no person at Blueprint stands between

findings.title: The new-job email says nothing about the job
findings.today: Every new-job email reads 'A site has posted a new job. Open it to see the job packet and respond.' No job type, place or readiness. A company must sign in to learn whether it is relevant.
findings.should: Subject and first line name the job type and country (and state if the owner allows): 'New job: Move materials, United States'.
findings.proposal: Build the subject and body from the card's category title and country, which every approved company already sees on the card.
findings.user_result: A company triages from its inbox; fewer wasted sign-ins; fewer unsubscribes.
findings.risk: Words must stay non-identifying; use only the fixed category and country.
findings.requirement_source: package E4 'Nothing about the site' (category and country are not about the site's identity)

findings.title: No email when the simulation becomes ready, and companies approved later never hear of open jobs
findings.today: The send happens once, when a job is first listed, only to companies that have already accepted the Terms signed in. An approved company not yet signed up is skipped for that job forever. Nothing tells anyone when the simulation package appears.
findings.should: One email when a job becomes Ready to test; a newly signed-in company sees a one-line 'N open jobs' on its first visit (it already sees the list).
findings.proposal: Add a second idempotent outbox row per company (key robot_team_job_ready:<job>:<company>) queued when storedCompanySimulation first exists; reuse the same dispatch gate.
findings.user_result: Companies learn the moment they can answer 'Tested it: can do'.
findings.risk: One more email per job; must respect the same opt-out.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine: once a job's simulation exists a company downloads it and tests

findings.title: The packet gives the country only, while the application asks for cities and states
findings.today: Job page and cards say 'United States'. The job stores city, state and postal code. A company cannot tell whether a job is in its area without emailing.
findings.should: The job shows state and country (never the city or address).
findings.proposal: Return the decrypted state with the country in countryOf and show 'Texas, United States'; add it to the sharing statement wording if the owner requires.
findings.user_result: A company decides 'in our area or not' from the packet.
findings.risk: State is coarse but more than today; the sharing statement does not list region, so the owner decides.
findings.requirement_source: privacy hard stop (no address); the country-only rule itself is from package E3

findings.title: Cards in the job list look alike
findings.today: Cards show a regex-picked category ('Move materials') and the country. Several identical cards; the lead must open each job.
findings.should: Each card shows the site's sentence, already redacted for companies, under the title.
findings.proposal: Add the redacted sentence (companyJobPage's sentence) to the card payload and render one line of it.
findings.user_result: A lead picks the relevant job from the list without opening each.
findings.risk: The card is the widest surface; the same redaction must run (it already does for the page).

findings.title: The application asks three questions nothing reads, and hides the one field the check needs
findings.today: Six required fields, three free text (jobs, robots, region). No rule reads jobs or robots; the region check compares against countries so 'Texas and Oklahoma' never matches. The website, the signal for 'website matches email', is optional and collapsed.
findings.should: Four fields: name, work email, company, company website (required, visible).
findings.proposal: Remove workWanted, robot and region from the form and schema (keep reading old records); make website required; drop the region check.
findings.user_result: Applying takes a fraction of the typing; the approver sees the two signals that matter.
findings.risk: The owner may want robots to judge borderline applicants; can ask in reply. Could come back.
findings.requirement_source: nobody (no rule reads them); website: guard robotTeamAccessFit.ts

findings.title: After approval: a password, a second Terms agreement and a details review before the first job
findings.today: Approval email, link, a screen with password, Terms box and collapsed name and company, then Create account. Terms are 'agreed' on the application too, though that tick never counts.
findings.should: The email-bound link signs the company in; first visit shows one 'I agree' press; nothing else.
findings.proposal: Redeem the invitation as a sign-in link (custom token) without a password; show CompanyTermsPrompt on first visit; delete the details review and the application's Terms line (replace with a Privacy notice).
findings.user_result: One fewer screen, no password, one Terms agreement instead of two.
findings.risk: Recovery without a password relies on 'Email me a new link', which exists. The signed-in Terms press must stay.

findings.title: A declined or waiting applicant is never told anything
findings.today: Only approval is emailed. The 'in review' and 'declined' screens need a signed-in account, and an applicant cannot have one. Silence means no, not yet, or unread.
findings.should: One 'not yet' email on decline, and a reply-by date on the receipt.
findings.proposal: Queue a fixed 'not yet' email on decline (same outbox path as approval); delete the unreachable status screens.
findings.user_result: A company knows where it stands.

findings.title: Nobody can see how long approval takes, and nothing reminds the owner
findings.today: One Slack message on a new application; no timer, reminder or measurement of applied-to-decided time, the slowest human link here.
findings.should: A daily line to the owner listing applications older than N days; the duration shown on the review page.
findings.proposal: Add an ops alert for robotTeamAccess with status applied and appliedAtIso older than N days.
findings.user_result: Companies are approved sooner; the owner sees the queue.
findings.risk: An alert the owner ignores is noise; one line a day.
findings.verify_how: Run the robotTeamAccess duration aggregate listed in the report.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine: Blueprint approves a company once

findings.title: The simulation package opens only in USD tools and does not explain the success rule
evidence: cmd: open_pkg.py on fixture package -> mujoco cannot open scene.usda (XML parse error); trimesh: file_type 'usdc' not supported; mjcf/urdf/obj/stl/glb in package: []
findings.today: USD and an optional PLY only. MuJoCo and trimesh cannot open any file. success_rule.json fields are unexplained and carry the retired runner's timing (120 Hz physics, 15 Hz control).
findings.should: A plain mesh (GLB or OBJ) of the collision room and object, one README line per rule field, no timing.
findings.proposal: In build_package, export room_collision and object to GLB with pxr (local, free); add README lines for destination_containment, settling and minimum_lift; drop 'timing'.
findings.user_result: MuJoCo, Gazebo and PyBullet teams can test without converting.
findings.risk: Larger zip; the size steps must drop the mesh before the look.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine: a company downloads the simulation and tests in its own tools

findings.title: The package is made from the dropped trial's scene, and its plain README is not live
evidence: cmd: git diff cbff06b44 HEAD -- website_company_simulation.py -> BUILDER_REVISION v3 live, v4 at HEAD
findings.today: Live packages use builder v3, whose 'could not prepare' note prints internal codes. The source is the trial's team scene half.
findings.should: Deploy v4; name the source as the website scene, not the trial half.
findings.proposal: Ship the current release; rename trial wording in the module and its plan reads.
findings.user_result: Companies read plain notes without internal codes.

findings.title: After an answer, the simulation-result form shows the previous 'Saved' message
findings.today: Switching to 'Report simulation result' after sending Interested shows 'Saved. The site sees this answer' before anything is sent.
findings.should: The message clears when the form changes.
findings.proposal: Key the message by mode or reset it on mode change.

findings.title: After answering, nothing says what happens next
findings.today: 'Saved. The site sees this answer, without your company's name.' The next step is only in grey small print.
findings.should: 'Saved. If the site asks to meet, we email you its contact details.'
findings.proposal: Change nextAction text per answer (Interested/Tested can do: the meet line; Need more details: the site is asked; Not a fit: nothing more).
findings.user_result: The company knows what to expect.
findings.risk: Copy only; must not promise a response.

findings.title: Two answer forms where one would do
findings.today: 'Respond' and 'Report simulation result' are separate forms with separate drafts; plus 'Add details' with three more fields.
findings.should: One form: five answers once the simulation is ready; optional earliest start and question.
findings.proposal: Render one radio group from COMPANY_RESPONSE_STATES filtered by simulation readiness; delete 'What you have checked'.
findings.risk: Companies may mix up Interested and Tested it: can do; labels are distinct. Could come back.

findings.title: At 390 px the sample job sits below a six-field form
findings.today: On a phone the stranger meets the application before the sample job.
findings.proposal: Move SampleJob above the application on narrow widths.
findings.user_result: The lead sees what it gets before typing.

findings.title: Dead 'no video' branch on the job page
findings.today: The page carries copy for a description-only job; the server never sends that state and a video is required since 2026-11-20.
findings.proposal: Remove NO_VIDEO_YET, ASK_FOR_VIDEO and the 'none' video state.
findings.requirement_source: retired: description-only jobs (owner direction 2026-11-20 requires video)

findings.title: Preference targeting fields and old application fields are stored with no use
findings.today: Interests, categories and requirements have no screen and no effect; supportedSystems, pilotPackage and testSite are carried forward from retired forms.
findings.should: Fields deleted from schema and writes.
findings.proposal: Drop them from the input schemas; leave old records unread.

findings.title: The approval confirm names a retired capability-matching review
findings.today: The owner confirms 'capabilities, task fit, and prerequisites'; Slack says 'early-access application', 'Wants to test on', 'Book the call'. Doctrine shows every job to every approved company, so the only question is whether this is a real deployment company.
findings.should: Confirm reads 'This is a real robot deployment company'; Slack line names company, email, website and the two checks.
findings.proposal: Rewrite the confirm and Slack text; drop the region check.
findings.user_result: The approver checks the one thing that protects the site.
findings.requirement_source: doctrine: Blueprint approves a company once

good_things.what: 'What this job packet does not show' list on the job page
good_things.why: Says plainly there was no site test, no safety review, no route measured; saves a question email.

good_things.what: Site identity never reaches a company
good_things.why: Sentence and done rule are redacted; the payload builder never reads name, address or contacts.
Same inputs give the same digest; every file scanned; all references resolve inside the zip (pxr: 0 unresolved).

good_things.what: Outcome questions with a confirm press
good_things.why: Email scanners cannot record answers; questions stop after a final answer.
Turning job emails off works and is tested (3 targeted tests passed).
No verify-your-email detour on the normal path.

owner_questions.question: May the job show the site's state (never the city or address) next to the country?
owner_questions.recommendation: Yes; add 'the state the site is in' to the sharing statement wording.

owner_questions.question: May a declined company get one fixed 'not yet' email (reversing 2026-11-19)?
How many days should an applicant wait at most before an answer?
owner_questions.recommendation: Three working days, shown on the receipt, with an alert to you after that.

not_covered: Real approval durations, company counts and email delivery (need the Firestore aggregates in the report)
A real job's simulation package and its physics schemas (privacy rule; fixture only)
The admin approval page rendered (read in code only)
